people.Pratipa: King of the Kuru line; husband of Sunanda.
people.Devapi: Eldest son of Pratipa; a skin ailment led him to renounce the throne and take to the forest as an ascetic.
people.Bahlika: Son of Pratipa; ruled the Bahlika kingdom. His descendants fought on the Kaurava side.
people.Shantanu: Youngest son of Pratipa; became king when Devapi renounced. Father of Bhishma.
people.Bhurishravas: Son of Somadatta; a mighty Kaurava warrior slain by Satyaki at Kurukshetra.
people.Bhishma: Born Devavrata; took a vow of lifelong celibacy so his father could marry Satyavati, hence 'Bhishma'. He was Prabhasa, the eighth and last of the eight Vasus, cursed to a long mortal life for stealing the sage Vasishtha's cow; his seven brother-Vasus, shown here as Ganga's other sons, she returned at once to heaven. Grandsire and regent of the Kurus; a chiranjivi who chose his own hour of death.

VasuDhara.name: Dhara
VasuDhara.note: A Vasu, deva of the earth; a brother-Vasu of Bhishma (Prabhasa), borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuDhruva.name: Dhruva
VasuDhruva.note: A Vasu, deva of the pole star; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuSoma.name: Soma
VasuSoma.note: A Vasu, deva of the moon; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuAha.name: Aha
VasuAha.note: A Vasu, deva of the day and the ethereal space; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuAnila.name: Anila
VasuAnila.note: A Vasu, deva of the wind; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuAnala.name: Anala
VasuAnala.note: A Vasu, deva of fire (Agni); borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuPratyusha.name: Pratyusha
VasuPratyusha.note: A Vasu, deva of the dawn; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

people.Vyasa: Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa, son of Satyavati and the sage Parashara before her marriage; arranger of the Vedas and composer of the Mahabharat. Biological father, through niyoga, of Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura.
people.Chitrangada: Elder son of Shantanu and Satyavati; a proud king slain young by a gandharva, leaving no heir.
people.Vichitravirya: Younger son of Shantanu and Satyavati; wed Ambika and Ambalika but died childless, prompting the niyoga that continued the line.
people.Dhritarashtra: Born blind to Ambika through Vyasa's niyoga; the elder prince, kept from the throne by his blindness. Father of the Kauravas.
people.Pandu: Born pale to Ambalika through Vyasa's niyoga; king of Hastinapura. A curse made his touch fatal to a wife, so his sons were god-begotten.
people.Vidura: Born to the maid Parishrami through Vyasa's niyoga; an incarnation of Dharma, wisest counsellor of the Kurus, never king by birth of a servant.
people.Duryodhana: Eldest of the hundred Kauravas; the crown prince whose enmity for the Pandavas drove the war. At his birth jackals howled, an omen he should be cast out.
people.Dushasana: Second Kaurava; dragged Draupadi into the assembly and tried to disrobe her, an outrage Bhima avenged by tearing open his breast.
people.Vikarna: The one Kaurava who spoke up for Draupadi's honour in the dice hall; reckoned the most righteous of the brothers.
people.Jarasandha: A Kaurava son (not to be confused with the king of Magadha of the same name).
people.Chitrasena: A Kaurava skilled with the mace, often at Duryodhana's side.

Dushala.note: The only daughter of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, born after the hundred sons; wed to Jayadratha, king of Sindhu.

people.Yuyutsu: Son of Dhritarashtra by the maid Sughada; the one son of that house to cross over and fight on the Pandava side.

Lakshmanaa.note: Daughter of Duryodhana; carried off by Krishna's son Samba, which nearly sparked a war.

LakshmanaK.name: Lakshmana
LakshmanaK.note: Son of Duryodhana (Lakshmana Kumara); slain by Abhimanyu inside the chakravyuha.

Yudhishthira.note: Eldest Pandava, begotten of Kunti by Dharma (Yama); the just king, never known to lie.

Bhima.note: Second Pandava, begotten of Kunti by Vayu; of superhuman strength, sworn to kill all hundred Kauravas.

Arjuna.note: Third Pandava, begotten of Kunti by Indra; the supreme archer, friend of Krishna, hearer of the Bhagavad Gita.

Nakula.note: Fourth Pandava, twin son of Madri by the Ashvins; matchless horseman and the handsomest of men.

Sahadeva.note: Youngest Pandava, twin son of Madri by the Ashvins; wisest of the brothers and a knower of the future.

people.Prativindhya: Son of Yudhishthira and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.
people.Sutasoma: Son of Bhima and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.
people.Shrutakarma: Son of Arjuna and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.
people.Shatanika: Son of Nakula and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.
people.Shrutasena: Son of Sahadeva and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.
people.Ghatotkacha: Son of Bhima and Hidimba; a rakshasa prince of great sorcery who grew to manhood in a day and died turning the tide of the war, drawing Karna's infallible weapon onto himself.
people.Barbarika: Son of Ghatotkacha; the archer of the three arrows who vowed to fight for whichever side was losing and so gave up his head to Krishna.
people.Abhimanyu: Son of Arjuna and Subhadra; the boy warrior who broke into the chakravyuha and was killed within it, leaving Uttara pregnant with the Kuru line's sole heir.
people.Parikshit: Son of Abhimanyu and Uttara; stillborn but revived by Krishna, he became the sole surviving heir and king of the Kurus after the war.
people.Janamejaya: Son of Parikshit; the king at whose serpent sacrifice the Mahabharat was first recited by Vaishampayana.

ShatanikaII.name: Shatanika
ShatanikaII.note: Son of Janamejaya (not to be confused with the Upapandava of the same name); he carried the Kuru throne into the age after the war.

people.Ashwamedhadatta: Son of Shatanika; a later Kuru king. The Puranas run the line on through several more kings to Kshemaka, its last.

Yama.name: Yama (Dharma)
Yama.note: Dharma, the deva of righteousness and lord of justice; father of Yudhishthira, who inherited his unwavering truth.

Vayu.name: Vayu Deva
Vayu.note: The deva of the wind; father of the mighty Bhima (and, in the earlier age of the Ramayan, of Hanuman).

Indra.name: Indra Deva
Indra.note: King of the devas, wielder of the thunderbolt; an Aditya, son of Aditi and Kashyap, and so a brother of Surya. Father of Arjuna, to whom he later gave celestial weapons.

Nasatya.note: One of the twin Ashvini Kumaras, devas of dawn and healing; father, by Madri, of Nakula.

Dasra.note: One of the twin Ashvini Kumaras, devas of dawn and healing; father, by Madri, of Sahadeva.
